export type User = {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  name: string;
  createdAt: string;
};

const users: User[] = [
  { id: "1", email: "ada@example.com", name: "Ada", createdAt: "2026-01-04" },
  { id: "2", email: "grace@example.com", name: "Grace", createdAt: "2026-02-11" },
];

export async function listUsers(): Promise<User[]> {
  return users;
}

export async function getUser(id: string): Promise<User | undefined> {
  return users.find((u) => u.id === id);
}

// TODO: there is no real session handling yet — the dashboard just picks the first user.
export async function getCurrentUser(): Promise<User | undefined> {
  return users[0];
}

content.text:
Creating a user now schedules a reminder job that logs 10 minutes later and retries if it fails. I haven't run it end to end, so the job itself is untested.

`npx tsc --noEmit` reports one error, in `src/app/layout.tsx` (`Cannot find name 'LayoutProps'`). I didn't touch that file and didn't check whether it was already failing. ESLint on `src` is clean.

I used Inngest. It works with Next.js route handlers and has built-in delays and retries. It also needs no credentials for local development.

- **Delay:** `src/inngest/functions.ts` defines `userReminder`, which triggers on a `notely/user.created` event. It waits 10 minutes with `step.sleep` and then logs the reminder.
- **Retries:** the function is set to `retries: 5`, with Inngest's default backoff. A retry doesn't repeat the 10-minute wait.
- **Serving:** `src/app/api/inngest/route.ts` serves the function, and `src/inngest/client.ts` holds the client.
- **Wiring:** `src/lib/users.ts` had no way to create a user, so I added `createUser({ email, name })`. It adds the user to the in-memory list and sends the event. If sending the event fails, that is logged and the user is still created.
- **Config:** `.env.example` has placeholder `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` and `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`. I added `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`, because `.env*` was ignored and the example file would otherwise stay out of git.

To try it locally:
1. Run `npm run dev`.
2. In another terminal, run `npx inngest-cli@latest dev -u http://localhost:3000/api/inngest`.
3. Call `createUser`, then watch the run in the dashboard at http://localhost:8288.

Nothing calls `createUser` yet, because there is no signup route or UI. Say if you want me to add one.
